title: For Loops
story: A for loop walks a list. The list can be words, a glob like *.log or a range like {1..5}.
goal: Print the name of every .log file in the current folder with its line count, like app.log: 3
hints: for f in *.log; do ... done expands the glob for you.

for f in *.log; do
  echo "$f: $(wc -l < "$f")"
done
socratic: Who expands *.log, you or the shell?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “For Loops”?
solution:
for f in *.log; do
  echo "$f: $(wc -l < "$f")"
done
